source.title: Towards practical quantum neural network diagnostics with neural tangent kernels
source.authors: Francesco Scala; Christa Zoufal; Dario Gerace; F. Tacchino

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It contains minor apparent typos and figure text extraction artifacts, but no material cutoff.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates learning-rate stability diagnostics on quantum neural networks, a new model setting, and reports training outcomes above the estimated critical learning rate.
record.gate_note: The paper studies QNNs trained on synthetic regression and classification tasks with MSE. Its CIFAR results, residual shortcuts, initialization comparisons, and classical-network training-error claims are not tested. Figure-only training curves are not reconstructed as numerical values. Cited classical results are not recorded as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study uses an initial-kernel stability bound to develop and validate QNN diagnostics. Its parameterized quantum circuits do not match the classical networks named in V1–V6. The experiment at 10 times the estimated critical rate reports oscillations, without establishing recovery, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, or divergence.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive initialization-based QNTK diagnostics for critical learning rate, average-error decay, and inference under frozen-kernel assumptions. Simulations give strongest agreement for sufficiently deep circuits and useful approximations for some shallow models; large parameter changes and incomplete convergence reduce agreement.
record.recipe_differences: Quantum parameterized circuits, synthetic datasets, MSE loss, and vanilla gradient descent; this is not the classical image-classification recipe in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different behavior by encoding frequency and ansatz: low-frequency and HVA-based QNNs appear slightly more resilient at ten times the estimated critical learning rate. QNTK approximation quality also varies with depth and parameter change.

fits_no_version.finding: On TFIM regression, QNNs trained at 10 times their QNTK-estimated critical learning rate exhibit severe oscillations. Low-frequency and HVA-based models appear somewhat more resilient. Relative parameter changes exceed 10%, violating the lazy-training approximation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initial-QNTK stability estimates can identify learning rates associated with unstable, non-lazy training in parameterized quantum circuits, with sensitivity to encoding and ansatz.

record.problems: The formal analysis assumes lazy training and a frozen QNTK. The above-critical-rate experiment uses 10ηcrit, described as an extreme setting; plotted training values are not extractable from the supplied figure text. The study uses synthetic quantum tasks rather than the classical benchmarks in the versions.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Results at η = ηcrit and figures reporting QNTK diagnostics or inference approximation do not measure the above-threshold training behavior named in V5.

untested.parts: All: classical convolutional networks, CIFAR training classification error, label corruption, model size, and training-recipe comparisons.
All: ReLU teacher-student networks, spurious local minima, and additional student neurons.
All: depth degradation in plain convolutional networks, residual shortcuts, and the special-initialization exceptions.
All: activation-matched initializations, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth.

All in the stated classical-network setting. No test of modestly supercritical recovery, the loss-rise/curvature-drop sequence, persistent sharpness near the stability threshold, or divergence from initially subcritical rates.
All: batch-normalization speed and learning-rate comparisons, and Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 5 contains final-loss summaries rather than loss trajectories demonstrating a catapult sequence. Oscillation and departure from lazy training should not be relabeled as divergence or failed recovery. Results at the critical rate and in the appendices do not supply tests of the stated versions.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, convolutional network size, and the stated early stopping and regularization comparisons.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks, batch normalization, depth-related training error, and the stated special-initialization and Fixup comparisons.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and very deep plain networks.

The study evaluates QNN training at its QNTK-estimated critical rate and at ten times that rate, but does not test wide classical networks, rates just above the limit, the catapult sequence of a brief loss rise followed by low loss, sharpness behavior, or divergence from below the threshold.
Batch normalization comparisons and Fixup training of residual networks without normalization.

rows.note: The text says this setting is in extreme conditions with severe oscillations around the loss landscape; the plotted final MSE is not available as an extractable numerical value.
